scope: Market network speeds behind the lab stress profile, WhatsApp usage phrasing, East African data-protection and influencer/advertising disclosure checks, and the 2026-09-25 model-currentness review, from Digital Research wave 2 (register 2026-09-24).
archive_policy: Archives were not created; archive status is NOT_ASSESSED. Facts come only from the Digital Research currentness registers of 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24. Nothing here is legal advice.

sources.title: UCC quality-of-service drive tests Aug-Sep 2024 (via Ecofin Agency, 2025-01-20)
sources.publisher: Uganda Communications Commission; summary by Ecofin Agency
sources.scope_and_limit: Mean mobile download MTN 16.3, Airtel 15.5, Lycamobile 5.3 Mbps in 30 towns at peak hours; latency 69-84 ms. Figures not verified against the UCC table (image); drive test, not a user median; about two years old.

sources.scope_and_limit: Median download 8.4 Mbps, upload 8.0, latency 192 ms; small self-selected browser sample, mixed desktop and mobile; not Ookla.

sources.scope_and_limit: WebFetch refused speedtest.net; Opensignal returned 403. NOT_ASSESSED; do not quote figures.

sources.scope_and_limit: Ookla median 45.37 Mbps and 50.63 Mbps (StatRanker); Ookla page inaccessible; no source found for 28 ms Kenya latency. Tanzania and Rwanda: no source found.

sources.title: Synthesis: 1.6 Mbps profile is not a measured median
sources.scope_and_limit: Every source found is above 1.6 Mbps; the profile is defensible only as a constrained or congested-tail stress profile (inference; the tail is not quantified).

sources.title: Synthesis: WhatsApp share-of-smartphone-users claim
sources.scope_and_limit: No source measures WhatsApp share of smartphone users for Uganda, Kenya, Tanzania or Rwanda; 90%+ figures found are unattributed internet-user estimates (Yazi); Pew 2023 adults survey implies Kenya below 90%.

sources.scope_and_limit: s.26 written opt-out from direct marketing, 14-day response; PDPO registration duty, 12-month validity (register 2026-09-23 PL-01). PDPO site rendered no content, so current fees and exemptions are unconfirmed. Not legal advice.

sources.title: Kenya Data Protection Act 2019 s.37 and Data Protection (General) Regulations 2021 regs 14-17; ODPC guidance

No s.37(3) guidelines found; ODPC influencer-disclosure guidance not found (register 2026-09-24 SRC-KE-DPA, SRC-KE-ODPC).

sources.scope_and_limit: Lineup includes Fable 5.1, Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5, Haiku 4.5 (retirement not sooner than 2026-10-15). Documentation catalogue, not this account's runtime availability.

claims.claim: The 1.6 Mbps / 300 ms lab profile is not a measured market median. Measured figures found are higher: UCC Uganda drive tests roughly 5-16 Mbps mean mobile download (Aug-Sep 2024, via Ecofin, unverified against the UCC table) and SpeedOf.Me Uganda 8.4 Mbps (H1 2026, small browser sample). It stays as a deliberate conservative throttled Slow-4G/3G stress profile for the constrained tail; the tail is not quantified (inference). Gate thresholds are not weakened.

Kenya mobile is roughly 45-50 Mbps median in 2025 Ookla snapshots (secondary reports; snapshot month unconfirmed). The earlier 28 ms Kenya latency has no source and is withdrawn. Supersedes the Kenya part of PERF-007.
Ookla Speedtest Global Index for Uganda, Tanzania and Rwanda and Opensignal for Uganda remain NOT_ASSESSED; no Tanzania or Rwanda speed source was found.

'WhatsApp is used by 90%+ of smartphone users in East Africa' is unsupported as worded. Say WhatsApp is a dominant messaging channel in East Africa, cite the best-attributed dated figure with its source and base (for example Pew 2023 adults survey, at least half of adults in every country surveyed incl. Kenya), and check the client's own audience data. No percentage is asserted.
